# Hardware

Plugin ID `hardware`. The physical host behind the cluster.

The Hardware page shows the physical host behind the cluster from its node-exporter and IPMI
series, read through the prometheus plugin: power draw, temperatures, fans and power supplies,
ZFS pools with their scrubs, and the SMART health of each drive bay. It also lists the machines
outside the cluster you name as up or down, by their node-exporter or a Gatus check. A ZFS pool
that is not online or whose last scrub found errors, a disk that fails SMART and a CPU at or
above the warning temperature become attention items on the Overview.

## What it shows

### Pages

| Page | Path |
|---|---|
| Hardware | `/hardware` |

### Panels on other pages

| Page | Panel | Id |
|---|---|---|
| Overview, KPI row (`overview.kpis`) | Power | `power` |
| Overview, KPI row (`overview.kpis`) | CPU temp | `cpu-temp` |

### Contributions

It contributes attention items, KPIs and the topology.

### Topics

Published on `/api/v1/stream` and `/api/v1/topics/{topic}`:

| Topic | Payload | What |
|---|---|---|
| `hardware.hosts` | `HostData` | The host's sensors, power, disks and pools. |
| `hardware.machines` | `MachinesData` | Machines outside the cluster, up or down. |

### Series

Chart series on `/api/v1/series`: `host.power`, `host.cpuTemp`, `host.cpu`, `host.mem`, `host.temps`, `host.fans`.

## Dependencies

A change to a plugin's settings restarts it and the plugins that require or use it.

- **Uses** [Prometheus-compatible](prometheus.md) when it runs.
- **Uses** [Proxmox VE](proxmox.md) when it runs.
- **Uses** [Gatus](gatus.md) when it runs.

## Settings

Every setting is under `plugins.hardware` in the config file and is also in the [configuration reference](../configuration.md#pluginshardware), with the rules for all of them: the layers, the `_FILE` form of each variable and secret references. _Restart_ marks a setting that applies only when dash restarts; a change to any other restarts the plugin in place.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Secret | Restart | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.hardware.type` | `DASH_PLUGINS_HARDWARE_TYPE` | string | - | no | no | The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name. |
| `plugins.hardware.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_HARDWARE_ENABLED` | boolean | - | no | no | false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). |
| `plugins.hardware.hosts` | `DASH_PLUGINS_HARDWARE_HOSTS` | list of objects (JSON) | - | no | no | The machine behind the cluster, as [{name, nodename, model, bays, fanMaxRPM, sensorAliases}]; every key is optional, and [{}] reads the Proxmox node, which needs the proxmox plugin to run (its URL, token ID and token secret set) unless nodename is set. One entry is supported for now. A JSON list in the environment. |
| `plugins.hardware.machines` | `DASH_PLUGINS_HARDWARE_MACHINES` | list of objects (JSON) | - | no | no | Machines outside the cluster to show as up or down, as [{name, nodeExporterNodename}] (up while their node-exporter is scraped) or [{name, gatusEndpoint}] (up while that Gatus check passes). A JSON list in the environment. |
| `plugins.hardware.selectors.nodeExporterJob` | `DASH_PLUGINS_HARDWARE_SELECTORS_NODE_EXPORTER_JOB` | string | `node-exporter` | no | no | The job label of the node-exporter targets, which the machines' up queries select. |
| `plugins.hardware.selectors.hwmonChip` | `DASH_PLUGINS_HARDWARE_SELECTORS_HWMON_CHIP` | string | `platform_coretemp_.*` | no | no | RE2 regular expression for the chip label of the CPU package temperature (node_hwmon_temp_celsius), e.g. platform_coretemp_.* for Intel. |
| `plugins.hardware.tempThresholds.warn` | `DASH_PLUGINS_HARDWARE_TEMP_THRESHOLDS_WARN` | integer | `85` | no | no | The CPU package temperature, in °C, from which the host is warning. Greater than zero and below crit. |
| `plugins.hardware.tempThresholds.crit` | `DASH_PLUGINS_HARDWARE_TEMP_THRESHOLDS_CRIT` | integer | `90` | no | no | The CPU package temperature, in °C, from which the host is critical. |
| `plugins.hardware.zfsScrubMetricPrefix` | `DASH_PLUGINS_HARDWARE_ZFS_SCRUB_METRIC_PREFIX` | string | - | no | no | Prefix of the ZFS scrub series: <prefix>_last_end_timestamp_seconds, <prefix>_last_errors and <prefix>_in_progress. Must be a valid metric name. Empty queries no scrub data and the pool cards show none. |

- The Hardware plugin reads the host's node from the running Proxmox plugin, so without
  `hosts[0].nodename` the Hardware row stays `unavailable` ("waiting for the Proxmox node name")
  until Proxmox runs (URL, token ID and token secret set).
- `hosts[].name` is the host's name in the web UI (default: the Proxmox node, then `nodename`).
- `hosts[].nodename` is the label of the host's node-exporter and IPMI series (default: the node
  of the running Proxmox plugin, that is `plugins.proxmox.node` or the discovered node; set it to
  run without a Proxmox token).
- `hosts[].model` is shown next to the name, e.g. `Example 2U`.
- `hosts[].bays` is the number of drive slots the Disks grid draws (0 to 128; 0 numbers the slots
  from 1, or from 0 when a disk sits in slot 0, up to the highest slot that holds a disk, at most
  128 slots, and above that the page lists the disks sorted).
- `hosts[].fanMaxRPM` is the top of the fan gauges (0 scales them to the fastest fan, and a gauge
  never ends below the speed a fan reports; the hosts payload calls it `fanMaxRpm`).
- `hosts[].sensorAliases` is `{inlet, exhaust}`, the text the names of the Inlet and Exhaust
  temperature sensors contain, ignoring case (`inlet` and `exhaust` when empty).
- In the environment:
  `DASH_PLUGINS_HARDWARE_HOSTS='[{"model":"Example 2U","bays":16,"fanMaxRPM":18000}]'`.
- A machine with `nodeExporterNodename` is up while the node-exporter with that `nodename` label
  is scraped. A `gatusEndpoint` is compared without regard to case; a check that does not exist,
  or no gatus plugin, counts as down. Each entry of `machines` has exactly one of the two, and the
  names are unique ignoring case and at most 64 bytes.

## Actions

None: the plugin only reads.

## Demo twin

With `DASH_DEMO=true` dash runs the plugin's demo twin instead: the same manifest, enabled and configured whatever the settings say, publishing made-up data from the fake lab in `internal/demo/world` and contacting nothing.
